reviewer: Codex, personal complete-final-answer read; no paid judge
primary_route: Primary proposed optogenetic pathway-necessity test during cue retrieval; evaluate the actual illumination site, physiological validation and behavioral controls selected in the answer.

checks.quote: # Optogenetic Test of Necessity of the P→Q Projection During Cue Retrieval
checks.reason: No explicit plan to consult prior detailed Methods/supplements or validated protocols before implementation and verify transfer of conditions. Generic calibration or a validated tool label does not meet M.

checks.quote: no illumination during the ITI
checks.reason: No off-window illumination condition tests the temporal specificity claim; merely omitting illumination outside retrieval is not a temporal control.

checks.quote: no carry-over onto subsequent light-off trials would indicate persistent motor disruption
checks.reason: This time-lock statement reverses the prediction: absence of carryover does not indicate a persistent disruption. It contradicts the following claim that carryover favors slowing.

checks.quote: Inject retrograde vector
checks.reason: No functional viral dose, delivered amount, expression timing or executable surgical/preparation calibration procedure.

checks.quote: or a behavioral probe
checks.reason: Behavioral interruption is allowed to replace physiological inhibition validation. Lowest power/duty and postmortem inspection also do not measure acute heating or establish target-engagement/calibration accuracy.

checks.quote: # Optogenetic Test of Necessity of the P→Q Projection During Cue Retrieval
checks.reason: No explicit primary trial denominator incorporating omissions or rule for corrupted/missing tracking/event measurements.

checks.quote: number of light-on vs. light-off trials per animal
checks.reason: Power targets trials rather than the number of independently allocated animals; animal-level variance/precision planning is absent.

checks.quote: locomotion as a time-varying covariate
checks.reason: Adjusting post-treatment movement does not identify a retrieval-specific effect without causal assumptions. No uncertainty intervals/multiplicity procedure support the multiple claims.

checks.quote: guarantees the animal's P→other projection is untouched
checks.reason: Projection-defined somatic expression does not spare collaterals of those same cells. O2 provides access to Q-projecting neurons, not exclusively Q-projecting neurons.

checks.quote: sweeping intensity and pulse protocol
checks.reason: No bounded intensity/duty exploration or independently defined physiological acceptance before lock; behavioral suppression is an allowed tuning target.

checks.quote: # Optogenetic Test of Necessity of the P→Q Projection During Cue Retrieval
checks.reason: Repeat-after-repair lacks explicit refreeze and fresh independent confirmatory data.

checks.quote: no significant light-on effect
checks.reason: Nonsignificance of controls does not establish negligible sensory/motor effects; no equivalence or meaningful-effect bounds define the necessity decision.

checks.quote: use as a confirmatory follow-up only
checks.reason: Terminal inhibition is only named, without an operational independently validated protocol. The primary soma result therefore lacks a valid orthogonal pathway test.

checks.quote: # Optogenetic Test of Necessity of the P→Q Projection During Cue Retrieval
checks.reason: Trial/light logs are useful but no complete raw file, stable identifier, calibration and exact processing/code/environment provenance manifest.

checks.quote: # Optogenetic Test of Necessity of the P→Q Projection During Cue Retrieval
checks.reason: Proposed randomized blinded animal/trial study with matched reporter and other-projection groups, postmortem targeting checks, movement/light probes and practical diagnostics. The central assertion that somatic projection-defined inhibition spares collateral output is false. Time-lock, post-treatment adjustment and null-control logic are also flawed, each charged under its specific criterion.
